subject: Sirius v2.4 tail-latency impacting PayFlux checkout
messages:
From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@payflux.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-12-18T13:22:00Z
Subject: SLA alert: Sirius v2.4 p95 spike impacting checkout

Hi Ben / Monica,

We're seeing a sustained p95 latency jump on model 'sirius-v2.4' that started ~12:40 UTC and is still ongoing. PayFlux checkout calls that hit the hosted Redwood endpoint are returning timeouts that map to user-facing checkout failures (we're seeing ~2.6% failed transactions over the last 30m). Key metrics: p95 jumped from ~210ms baseline to ~1.9s, error-rate to 2.6%, traffic is steady at ~130 rps to the route.

Can Redwood pin our traffic back to the previous stable variant (sirius-v2.3) or authorize a temporary SLA carveout while you investigate? We need a plan ASAP — Commerce ops is holding a mitigation window at 15:00 UTC.

Attached: a short CSV with p95 samples and a small trace we captured.

Thanks,
Tom Liu
Head of Integrations — PayFlux

(attachment: payflux_p95_sample.csv)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-18T14:00:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA alert: Sirius v2.4 p95 spike impacting checkout

Tom — thanks for the heads up and for the samples. We're on it. Immediate plan I propose:

1) Internal triage and mitigation: request SRE to create a short-lived traffic split (70% -> v2.3, 30% -> v2.4) to reduce customer impact while we investigate.
2) If the split does not materially improve p95 within 30m, authorize a full pin back to sirius-v2.3.
3) Request approval for a temporary SLA exception window covering 14:00–18:00 UTC while we remediate; we'll provide hourly status updates.

Monica: can you coordinate the customer comms and confirm PayFlux is OK with the 70/30 split as a first step?
Soojin/Vivek/Marissa: asking ops/infra for technical assessment and rollback/runbook readiness. We need a yes/no on an immediate pin (20m window for change).

I'll keep this thread as the single source of truth.

Ben Carter

- We can perform a traffic split or a full rollback, but full rollback requires a 20–30 minute coordination window (canary drain + cache warm-up).
- Need confirmation that PayFlux accepts potential transient errors during the topology change.
- Request SRE traces and model-variant activation logs for the 12:00–13:00 UTC window (to look for kernel/hardware hot paths or quantization patch interactions).

Date: 2026-12-19T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA alert: Sirius v2.4 p95 spike impacting checkout

Team / Tom — brief technical summary from SRE after initial forensics:

- Observed pattern: p95 spike correlates with a routing change and an internal batching tweak rolled into v2.4 (batch window increased from 8ms to 16ms). This increased tail latency significantly for short-sequence requests (typical PayFlux checkout).
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~12% shortly after deploy; that aligns with an auxiliary cache invalidation in the runtime.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
A) 70/30 traffic split to sirius-v2.3 (quickest, low risk).
B) Rollback to v2.3 (higher disruption during switch due to cache warm-up, but full remediation).
C) Patch in-place: revert batching change and push v2.4.1 (requires build/test; ETA ~3–4h).

Runbook & artifacts attached. My recommendation: start with A (70/30) immediately, monitor for 30–45m. If p95 does not drop at least 60% relative to the current spike, escalate to B. If PayFlux gives hard requirement for full rollback now, we can do B but we need the green light and a maintenance window.

Attachments: p95_sirius_v2-4_report.csv, sirius_rollback_runbook.pdf

Soojin Lee
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@payflux.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-19T16:05:00Z
Subject: Action plan: temporary split to mitigate Sirius v2.4 tail latency 

Tom — thanks for your patience. Per SRE/Infra recommendation we propose the following immediate mitigation and next steps: 

1) Implement 70% traffic -> sirius-v2.3, 30% -> sirius-v2.4 at 16:30 UTC today. We'll monitor p95, error-rate, and user success for 2 hours.
2) If p95 (PayFlux route) does not improve by >=60% within 45 minutes, we will escalate to a full rollback to v2.3 (expected 20–30 minute window).
3) If the split stabilizes metrics, we will follow with a v2.4.1 patch (revert batching change) and schedule a controlled rollout.
4) Requesting a temporary SLA exception for the 14:00–18:00 UTC window for PayFlux to avoid breach; we'll send hourly status notes and a final incident report.

Please reply with an explicit OK to proceed with the 70/30 split (Tom: "OK to split"), or say if you want us to perform an immediate full rollback. If we don't hear from you by 16:20 UTC we'll hold and wait for explicit consent.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference
